definitions.explanation: The practice of cutting away dead or overgrown branches or stems to promote healthy growth and maintain the shape of plants and trees.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{木|き}の{剪定|せんてい}をした。
examples.english: I pruned the trees in the garden.

examples.japanese: {剪定|せんてい}は{冬|ふゆ}に{行|おこな}うのが{良|よ}い。
examples.english: It's best to do pruning in winter.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}に{松|まつ}の{剪定|せんてい}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I asked a craftsman to prune the pine tree.

notes:
{剪定|せんてい} refers to the practice of pruning plants and trees.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {剪定|せんてい}する (to prune)
- {剪定|せんてい}を{行|おこな}う (to carry out pruning)
- {剪定|せんてい}{ばさみ|はさみ} (pruning shears)

TYPES OF PRUNING:
- {強剪定|つよせんてい} (heavy pruning)
- {軽剪定|かるせんてい} (light pruning)
- {透|す}かし{剪定|せんてい} (thinning cuts)
- {切|き}り{戻|もど}し (cutting back)

TOOLS:
- {剪定|せんてい}ばさみ (pruning shears)
- {剪定|せんてい}のこぎり (pruning saw)
- {高枝切|たかえだき}りばさみ (pole pruner)

GARDENING NOTE:
In Japan, pine tree ({松|まつ}) pruning is a specialized skill, and professional gardeners ({植木屋|うえきや}) are often hired for this work.
